question: What is the primary objective of dietary counselling in clinical and community settings?

options.A: Enforcing strict institutional meal schedules on hospitalized patients
options.B: Prescribing pharmaceutical vitamin supplements for acute deficiencies
options.C: Diagnosing underlying metabolic disorders through laboratory analysis
options.D: Facilitating voluntary adoption of health-promoting eating behaviors

explanation: Dietary counselling focuses on guiding individuals toward sustainable and healthy food choices rather than merely handing out rigid meal instructions. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T002#GNS227_U7_T002_h1)

question: Why must dietary counselling in Nigeria incorporate cultural and socioeconomic factors?

options.A: To eliminate the need for biochemical blood investigations
options.B: To satisfy strict international hospital accreditation mandates
options.C: To reduce the overall duration of the hospital stay
options.D: To ensure recommendations align with local staple foods and financial realities

explanation: Patients are far more likely to adhere to dietary advice when recommendations respect their cultural food preferences and economic capacity. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T002#GNS227_U7_T002_h1)

question: Which tool is commonly utilized during individual dietary counselling to evaluate a client's recent food intake?
explanation: A 24-hour recall allows the clinician to record everything the patient consumed over the previous day, offering insight into typical eating patterns. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T002#GNS227_U7_T002_h2)

question: What is the primary advantage of choosing a one-on-one format over a classroom setting for a newly diagnosed diabetic patient?

options.A: It permits highly customized dietary planning based on personal medical history
options.B: It is significantly faster and requires fewer resources
options.C: It completely prevents the occurrence of dietary non-compliance
options.D: It eliminates the need for any follow-up clinical appointments

explanation: Individual sessions focus exclusively on one person's unique clinical parameters, lifestyle constraints, and specific metabolic needs. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T002#GNS227_U7_T002_h2)

question: What is a major benefit of group dietary counselling compared to individual sessions?

options.A: Instantaneous customization of rare metabolic formulas
options.B: Absolute confidentiality regarding sensitive medical diagnoses
options.C: Complete elimination of facilitator bias during discussions
options.D: Provision of peer support and shared experiential learning

explanation: Group settings foster a community environment where members encourage one another and share practical tips for overcoming everyday dietary hurdles. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T002#GNS227_U7_T002_h3)

question: A clinic organizes a weekly nutrition class for pregnant women with gestational diabetes. Which challenge should the nurse facilitator be most prepared to manage?

options.A: Complete absence of shared clinical experiences among attendees
options.B: Impossibility of addressing basic nutritional principles in a room
options.C: Dominant personalities overshadowing quieter group members
options.D: Immediate drop in institutional operational costs

explanation: Group dynamics can sometimes be skewed by vocal participants, requiring the facilitator to actively draw out quieter individuals. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T002#GNS227_U7_T002_h3)

question: Therapeutic dietary counselling is primarily indicated for which category of individuals?

options.A: Patients with established acute or chronic medical pathologies
options.B: General community members seeking general wellness tips
options.C: Healthy school-age children participating in sports
options.D: Corporate workers attending an annual health retreat

explanation: Therapeutic counselling is specifically designed for disease management where specialized nutrition is critical to halting or treating pathology. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T002#GNS227_U7_T002_h4)

question: Why is precision in dietary counselling critical for a patient diagnosed with advanced chronic kidney disease?

options.A: Dietary errors can precipitate dangerous electrolyte imbalances like hyperkalemia
options.B: Patients require strict instruction on commercial sports beverage intake
options.C: Kidney failure patients always require high-sodium meal plans
options.D: Nutritional restriction has no impact on renal filtration rates

explanation: Failing to restrict potassium or phosphorus in advanced renal disease can rapidly lead to life-threatening cardiac and metabolic emergencies. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T002#GNS227_U7_T002_h4)

question: What is the primary focus of community and preventive nutrition counselling?

options.A: Performing complex metabolic surgery on morbidly obese clients
options.B: Promoting health and preventing disease onset in populations
options.C: Administering intravenous nutrition to comatose patients
options.D: Managing acute surgical complications in intensive care units

explanation: Preventive counselling targets communities and healthy individuals to stop lifestyle diseases before they manifest clinically. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T002#GNS227_U7_T002_h5)

question: Which activity best exemplifies a community-level preventive nutrition intervention in a rural Nigerian setting?

options.A: Adjusting the exact insulin dosage for a hospitalized diabetic teenager
options.B: Prescribing total parenteral nutrition for a surgical bowel resection
options.C: Conducting a private psychiatric evaluation for an eating disorder
options.D: Holding a market-square demonstration on preparing nutrient-dense local weaning foods

explanation: Market demonstrations reach the broader community to educate caregivers on preventing malnutrition using accessible local ingredients. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T002#GNS227_U7_T002_h5)

question: Which characteristic best defines a directive counselling approach?

options.A: The client makes all clinical decisions without professional input
options.B: The counselor takes a leading, expert-driven role in prescribing solutions
options.C: The session is conducted entirely through digital text messaging
options.D: The focus remains exclusively on group dynamics rather than individuals

explanation: In directive counselling, the healthcare provider gives clear instructions and structured plans for the patient to follow. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T002#GNS227_U7_T002_h6)

question: When is a directive dietary counselling approach most appropriate in clinical practice?

options.A: When managing an acute medical crisis requiring strict dietary control
options.B: When exploring deep-seated emotional barriers to overeating
options.C: When a healthy adult wants general wellness tips for marathon training
options.D: When a patient resists all forms of professional healthcare authority

explanation: Emergency or critical clinical situations leave little room for exploratory dialogue and demand clear, immediate instructions. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T002#GNS227_U7_T002_h6)

question: What is a primary advantage of tele-counselling in modern healthcare delivery?

options.A: Guaranteeing universal high-speed internet access for all patients
options.B: Completely eliminating the need for any clinical documentation
options.C: Replacing the physical nursing assessment with automated artificial intelligence
options.D: Expanding access to specialist care for remote populations

explanation: Tele-counselling bridges geographical divides, allowing clients in rural areas to consult with healthcare professionals without traveling long distances. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T002#GNS227_U7_T002_h7)

question: Which factor represents a potential limitation when conducting virtual dietary counselling sessions?

options.A: Mandatory hospitalization of every patient utilizing the app
options.B: Excessive physical contact between the nurse and the client
options.C: Immediate elimination of all patient compliance challenges
options.D: Potential digital literacy barriers and limited access to technology

explanation: Not all patients possess smartphones, reliable internet, or the technical skills required to navigate virtual healthcare platforms effectively. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T002#GNS227_U7_T002_h7)
